title: Affineness of smooth groups with semisimple fibres over a Dedekind base
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one and $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite presentation. Group scheme means a scheme over $S$ with multiplication, inverse and identity satisfying the group diagrams; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Suppose that for every algebraically closed field $k$ and homomorphism $B\to k$, the geometric fibre $H_k$ is a connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] affine semisimple $k$-group. Here semisimple means that there is no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup; solvable means that successive commutator subgroups become trivial. Then $H\to S$ is affine, meaning that the inverse image of every affine open of $S$ is affine. Smoothness, finite presentation, spectra and affineness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. No splitness, choice of a torus, prescribed root datum, or generic-fibre identification is assumed; the trivial group is included.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-relative-adjoint] to $H\to S$. The ring $B$ is nonzero and Noetherian, and $H$ is smooth, separated and finitely presented as required. It gives a finite projective module $E$, a smooth separated affine finite-presentation group $L=\operatorname{GL}_S(E)$, and a finite-type group homomorphism $a=\operatorname{Ad}_H:H\to L$. This construction requires no affineness of $H$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.3.16, p.229, construction of the adjoint action; relative tangent formulation made explicit.

proof.text: Fix any algebraically closed field $k$ and map $B\to k$. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-group-relative-adjoint] identifies $a_k$ with the adjoint representation on $T_eH_k$. By hypothesis $H_k$ is a connected affine semisimple group; its smooth finite-type structure is inherited from the given smooth finite-presentation family. Therefore [lem-sfb-semisimple-adjoint-kernel-finite] says that the scheme-theoretic kernel of $a_k$ is finite over $k$. This holds for every such $k$, including geometric generic fibres and positive-characteristic fibres; it asserts scheme-theoretic finiteness, not etaleness.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.3.16, p.229, finite geometric kernels by classical semisimple theory.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], both $H\to S$ and $L\to S$ are flat, since both are smooth. Both are of finite type: their finite presentations give finite sets of algebra generators on the defining finite affine covers. They are separated, $a$ is a finite-type homomorphism, and step 2 supplies every finite geometric kernel required by [lem-sfb-dedekind-finite-kernel-hom-affine]. The base is the spectrum of exactly the Noetherian integrally closed one-dimensional domain in that lemma. Apply it to conclude that $a:H\to L$ is affine.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.3.16, p.229, the Dedekind-base homomorphism affineness input.

proof.text: The structure morphism $L\to S$ is affine by [lem-sfb-smooth-group-relative-adjoint]. The structure morphism of $H$ is the composite $H\xrightarrow{a}L\to S$, because $a$ is an $S$-homomorphism. Both factors are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-composition] makes this composite affine. This is the required inverse-image-of-affine-opens conclusion, also when $H$ is the trivial group and $E=0$.

Source checked: Conrad's Reductive group schemes, fetched read-only. Prop. 6.3.16's proof (printed p.229) is: Ad has finite geometric kernels by the classical theory, so it is quasi-finite; a quasi-finite homomorphism of separated flat finite-type groups over a Dedekind base is affine; GL is affine. Prop. 3.3.8 (p.102) says ker Ad is the centre. The 4 item steps follow that proof exactly and the statement is unchanged. Step 1: smooth-group-relative-adjoint; its hypotheses (nonzero Noetherian base, smooth separated fp group) all hold. Step 2: its base-change clause plus semisimple-adjoint-kernel-finite; smooth and finite type of H_k come from that clause, connected/affine/semisimple from the item. Step 3: lem-pc-smooth-flat (mathlib) for flatness, fp gives finite type, then dedekind-finite-kernel-hom-affine applies. Step 4: affine GL and lem-weil-pbc-affine-composition (mathlib). The two tool uses are Mathlib leaves; accepted. No SGA is cited. All new nodes are true and statement-only. Relative adjoint: omega is finite projective, the dual-number tangent identification needs no affineness, base change holds, E=0 works. Kernel finiteness: if the reduced identity component of ker Ad were nontrivial, its torus would lie in the finite Z(G)^0. Tested on mu_p in SL_p (char p), PGL_2 in char 2 and the trivial group. Dedekind lemma: finite geometric kernels plus finite type give quasi-finite, matching Conrad. Tested on Spec K in S, an open subgroup of a constant group missing a special-fibre point, and the identity of an elliptic curve.
